# tidymst

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/tidymst/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/tidymst/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

tidymst reads microscale thermophoresis (MST) data from NanoTemper's
software into tidy data frames, and analyses them:

* Read MST traces, capillary scans, dose-response data and fits with
  `read_mst()` and friends, from either the Excel files exported by
  MO.Affinity Analysis or the project files saved by MO.Control (`.moc`) and
  MO.Affinity Analysis (`.nta`). Everything is read into the same standard
  columns, with concentrations in molar.
* Recalculate Fnorm from the traces with any hot and cold windows, using
  `mst_fnorm()`.
* Fit Kd and Hill binding models with `mst_fit()`, and get the coefficients
  and curves with `mst_coefs()` and `mst_curve()`.
* Convert responses to delta Fnorm and fraction bound with `mst_normalise()`.
* Plot traces and dose-response curves with `mst_plot_traces()` and
  `mst_plot_dose_response()`, or with your own ggplot2 code.

## Installation

Install the development version of tidymst from GitHub with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("BradyAJohnston/tidymst")
```

## Example

Read the MST traces exported from MO.Affinity Analysis, calculate Fnorm for
the capillaries that weren't marked as outliers, and fit a Kd:

```{r}
#| label: example
#| message: false
library(tidymst)
library(dplyr)

traces <- read_mst_traces(tidymst_example("dppr10-cy5_traces.xlsx"))

fnorm <- traces |>
  filter(included, target == "atpH-fl") |>
  mst_fnorm(hot = c(19, 20))

fits <- mst_fit(fnorm, .by = target)
mst_coefs(fits)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot
#| fig-height: 3.5
mst_plot_dose_response(fnorm, fits)
```

## Reading project files

You don't need to export anything: the same functions read the project files
that NanoTemper's software saves. An MO.Affinity Analysis project (`.nta`)
holds the raw measurements and your analysis, including which capillaries are
outliers and the fits:

```{r}
#| label: project
project <- tidymst_example("dppr10-cy5.nta")

read_mst_dose_response(project) |>
  select(target, ligand_concentration, response, included)

read_mst_fit(project) |>
  select(target, model, fixed, kd, kd_std_error)
```

An MO.Control project (`.moc`) holds the measurements only, so it gives
traces and capillary scans.

See `vignette("tidymst")` for a full walk-through, including how to make
your own plots.
